newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q1 GDP DATA.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Q1 GDP DATA.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to final UK gross domestic product data for the first quarter. The figures showed a quarterly rise of 0.9 percent and an annual rise of 3.1 percent, compared with the rises of 0.9 and 3.0 percent last reported.
Marian Bell, Royal Bank of Scotland - the upward revision reflects greater activity in the service sector of the economy.
But overall "it does not look from these figures as if the economy has accelerated in the early part of this year".
Bell said the data justified recent rises in interest rates but did not point to the need for further rises.

ROB HAYWARD, BANK OF AMERICA -"GDP is obviously unchanged but the interesting thing is that consumer spending is driving the economy forward and the savings ratio fell to 10.4 percent from 11.4. The savings ratio is an indication of consumer confidence, where people are more inclined to spend than save. The fall would be consistent with the idea that consumer confidence is picking up and after falling in the first quarter it looks very likely that it will continue to do so in the second and third quarters. Therefore consumer spending is likely to remain very robust right the way through the year."

DAVID OWEN OF DRESDNER KLEINWORT BENSON - "They were very much in line with expectations. We were looking at roughly around 1.3 in Q2...It doesn't change our view. "The current account figures were very much better than expected and on balance we should be very bullish for sterling." UK current account data for the first quarter were also released and showed a surplus of 1.459 billion stg, up from 508 million in the fourth quarter of 1996. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5109
